source.author: hor
source.text: ipse ego, qui nullos me affirmo scribere versus, invenior Parthis mendacior, et prius orto sole vigil calamum et chartas et scrinia posco, navem agere ignarus navis timet; habrotonum aegro non audet nisi qui didicit dare; quod medicorum est promittunt medici ; tractant fabrilia fabri: scribimus indocti doctique poemata passim.
source.text_original: ipse ego, qui nullos me affirmo scribere versus, / invenior Parthis mendacior, et prius orto / sole vigil calamum et chartas et scrinia posco, / navem agere ignarus navis timet; habrotonum aegro / non audet nisi qui didicit dare; quod medicorum est / promittunt medici ; tractant fabrilia fabri:  / scribimus indocti doctique poemata passim.
source.text_english: I myself, who claim to write no verses, am found more deceitful than the Parthians, and before the sun has risen I am awake and ask for my pen, my papers, and my writing case; the man who does not know how to steer a ship fears to run a ship; only he who has learned how to give wormwood dares give it to the sick; what belongs to doctors, doctors promise; craftsmen handle craftsmen’s work: unlearned and learned alike write poems everywhere.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: Sola scripturarum ars est, quam sibi omnes passim uindicent: scribimus indocti doctique poemata passim.
reuse.text_original: Sola scripturarum ars est, quam sibi omnes passim uindicent: scribimus indocti doctique poemata passim.
reuse.text_english: The art of the Scriptures is the only one that everyone everywhere claims for himself: unlearned and learned alike we write poems everywhere.
